answer: A scripted farm therefore has to pad 219 submissions and hold each member open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which forfeits the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. Because the timing is published against the vault challenge, the summit audit can replay the nectar history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 27 times over for the same share of the pool. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
